title: Tulip trio in cross-stitch
subtitle: Three tulips in red, yellow, and pink on 14-count Aida
excerpt: A tulip trio is a 80-by-70 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. Three tulip heads in red, yellow, and pink share a simple green stem-and-leaf base and use nine floss colours. The horizontal grouping finishes at about 14 x 13 cm and suits a 15 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. Tulip motifs are among the oldest recurring subjects in European needlework.

content.text: A tulip trio is an 80-by-70 stitch piece on 14-count
. Three tulip heads sit side by side, red at left, yellow at centre, pink at right, on a shared base of two greens. Nine
colours cover the whole piece. A short
line on each stem makes the narrow stems crisp where a full-cross column would look blocky.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white or cream
items.substitutions: Pale blue Aida suggests a spring sky setting

content.text: Find the centre of the fabric. The chart centre falls on the yellow tulip head at centre. Begin there with the medium yellow (3821) and work the full head before moving to the adjacent tulips.
Stitch each tulip head completely, all colours in that head, before moving to the next flower. This avoids navigating between three separate colour areas at once.
Work the leaves and stems in the two greens (522 and 520) once all three heads are done. The curved leaf shapes are simply blocks of full crosses; no shaping stitches are needed.
Add back-stitch stem lines in 520 on the narrow sections between the leaf base and the flower head.
Wash and press face-down. Display in the hoop or frame with a white or cream mount. Works well as a companion piece to other botanical stems.

items.symptom: The three tulip heads are at different heights
items.cause: Each tulip was started independently without first checking that the stem bases align on the same counted row.
items.fix: Establish the base row for all three stems before stitching any petals. Mark the row with a single anchor stitch on each stem position, then work all three stems to the same height before adding the heads.

items.symptom: The tulip petals look stripy across the colour blend
items.cause: The pale and mid tones were worked in separate blocks rather than in alternating rows.
items.fix: Work petal shading in horizontal rows that alternate between pale and mid tones in the transition band. Once the blend rows are in, step back and check the gradation looks smooth at arm's length.

content.text: The peony bloom in this sub-category has more colour gradation and a higher stitch count. Try it once multi-colour groupings feel manageable.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.

A solid outline stitch worked in a single strand along the back-stitch layer of the chart. You stitch backwards along the line one stitch at a time, each stitch finishing where the previous one started.
